lines.text: Thirty days. One dollar. And Benny has to turn it into ten thousand.
Because this morning, his mom slapped a dollar on the table, and a note on the fridge.
Ten thousand dollars in thirty days, or you're moving out. Love, Mom.
Benny's assets. One dollar. A phone at three percent. And a bike with no seat.
His business experience? He once traded a fidget spinner for a slice of pizza.
So he rides the seatless bike to the store. Standing up. The whole way.
At the dollar store, he finds it. A bag of twenty lollipops. For one dollar.
The plan. Twenty lollipops at a quarter each is five dollars. That's a four hundred percent profit.
He sets up at the park. His first customer is a toddler.
The toddler offers ten cents. Benny says twenty five. The toddler walks away. Benny chases the toddler.
Then he sees her. An eight year old with a lemonade stand, a card reader, and a business plan.
Two dollars a cup. And she has a line.
But then soccer practice ends. Twenty sweaty kids. Zero snacks.
Benny sells out in four minutes.
Day one. Five dollars. He is officially five times richer.
Only nine thousand, nine hundred and ninety five to go.
So here's where you come in. Buy five more bags of lollipops? Or buy a bucket and a sponge, and start washing cars? Comment one word. Day two starts with your choice.
